 Follow How SC teachers can get up to $27,500 in student loan forgiveness
 Baker Maultsby, Spartanburg Herald-Journal Mon, November 2, 2026 at 10:06 AM UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. With teacher pay generally considered to be low and turnover in the profession is relatively high , South Carolina lawmakers have created a program to provide financial incentives for teachers to stay in public education.
 The General Assembly has set aside $10 million for the South Carolina Student Loan Corporation to offer teachers the opportunity to refinance outstanding educational debt to a fixed 2% rate.
 In select high-need districts, teachers can apply for loan forgiveness up to $27,500. In the Upstate, those school systems include Spartanburg districts 3 and 7, Anderson districts 2 and 3, Cherokee County and Union County.
 Spartanburg County School District 7 is one of the Upstate districts where qualifying teachers can apply for outstanding educational debt forgiveness through the South Carolina Student Loan Corporation. Funding came through a proviso authored by Rep. Neal Collins (R-Pickens).
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "I believe public education is the foundation for the success of our state's young people. This program is intended to provide financial support for teachers to keep them in the classroom," Collins said in a prepared statement. "This is our way of showing them their service is important to the people, especially the children, of South Carolina."
 Teachers can apply online through the South Carolina Student Loan website .
 For qualifying teachers in the districts where loan forgiveness is available, South Carolina Student Loan will absorb up to $27,500 in outstanding debt and write off 20% a year over five years.
 The hope is that those teachers will continue teaching in public schools for at least that five-year period.
 Advertisement Advertisement In the meantime, the low-interest refinancing for all of the qualifying teachers is "absolutely money in their pockets," said Ray Jones, who serves as chief products officer with SC Student Loan.
 Kira Reaves, chief human resources officer with Spartanburg School District 7, said the fund will "provide meaningful economic relief to those who give so much every day."
 More: Meet the Ingles Amazing Teacher for the month: Christina Banks 
 "Anything that can help educators with repayment of loans can really make a big difference," said Dena Crews, president of the South Carolina Education Association , a membership group that advocates for teachers.
 Advertisement Advertisement Jones said he hopes state lawmakers will add to the fund once the dollars currently available are gone.
 "But that's not guaranteed, so I would suggest that interested teachers go ahead and get in on it," he said.
